Most of the weight differences are tiny but appear almost everywhere, with about three quarters of elements shifted by a few ulp and a maximum near 1e-3. That pattern looks like full fine-tuning with Adam, where updates are roughly uniform across tensors. A maximum change around 0.0012 would fit a learning rate near 1e-5 over about a hundred steps.

Adam's per-element updates come out roughly uniform in magnitude, so the raw norm of the diff tells me little. I need to look at directional structure instead, so I'll run SVD on each diff matrix to check how low-rank it is, since Adam noise tends to be high-rank while any real signal might sit in a few directions. I also notice the norm weights barely moved, which could be bf16 rounding swallowing changes smaller than their ulp.

Down_proj seems to have smaller magnitude weights, which would explain its larger median ulp of 3-4 versus about 2 elsewhere, and the lower share of unchanged elements. Next I want to test how low-rank each diff is by comparing the singular value spectrum to what pure noise would produce, since real signal should appear as outliers.

content.text:
The diff is spread over everything: about 75% of the elements of every matrix differ, by a median of 2–4 bf16 ulps, with maxima near 1.2e-3 in all matrices. That is the signature of full fine-tuning with an Adam-type optimizer, where every coordinate moves by roughly ±lr per step. So raw norms and "fraction changed" carry almost no information. The norm vectors barely changed, since their bf16 ulp is too coarse. The real signal has to be found as *structured* (low-rank, coherent) directions on top of high-rank Adam noise.

Next I'll look at the singular-value spectrum of each A−B matrix (q/k/v/o, gate/up/down). I'll compare the top singular values with the bulk of the spectrum (Marchenko–Pastur-like noise edge) to find matrices that carry coherent low-rank changes. This still only locates the difference, so it gives no evidence on A vs B.

```python
A = Checkpoint("A"); B = Checkpoint("B")
os.makedirs("/work", exist_ok=True)
names=["self_attn.q_proj","self_attn.k_proj","self_attn.v_proj","self_attn.o_proj","mlp.gate_proj","mlp.up_proj","mlp.down_proj"]
res={}
for L in range(18):
    line=f"L{L:2d} "
    for n in names:
        k=f"model.layers.{L}.{n}.weight"
        d=A.get(k)-B.get(k)
        s=np.linalg.svd(d,compute_uv=False)
        res[(L,n)]=s
        # ratio top1 / median singular, and top1/ top10
        line+=f"{n.split('.')[-1][:4]}:{s[0]/np.median(s):5.2f}/{s[0]/s[5]:4.2f} "
    print(line)
np.save("/work/svals.npy", np.array([res[(L,n)][:20] for L in range(18) for n in names]))
```
